inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London on Saturday to protest the far-right, coming together under the Together Alliance in a broad coalition of trade unions, anti-racism campaigners, and Muslim representative bodies. This follows just six months after one of Britain's largest-ever far-right demonstrations and arrives weeks before key local elections. To me this turnout represents communities pushing back against the deep structural inequalities and institutional failures that have allowed discrimination and hate to spread, threatening vulnerable groups and workers alike. It's a clear demand for real reform to root out the historical injustices fueling division and to protect labor rights and minority communities from rising bigotry.
